claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Nucleus, VI-1' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Element summary, I-11'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Nucleus, VI-1' then '  Element summary, I-11'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: I compared the 300 dpi render of printed page B-58 with page-970.md. Every entry and page reference matches, including 'Nucleus, VI-1' followed by the indented 'Element summary, I-11'. In the source, each entry sits on its own line, sub-entries are indented two spaces, and wrapped continuations such as 'VI-104' are indented four. So the line boundaries and the main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are both still in the transcription. The only complaint is that a Markdown renderer would join these bare lines into one paragraph, which is formatting and presentation, not content. Nothing is missing, misquoted or changed in meaning. The difference from pages 961-962, which use '- ' list markers, is a formatting inconsistency in this informative index, not a content discrepancy.
